nodes.description:
Jira Issue DHIS2-22296: Org unit merge silently deletes the target's own data values when the target already has data
Type: Bug | Status: In Review | Priority: Highest
Components: [API] Other
Description: Prerequisite : a user with  F_ORGANISATION_UNIT_MERGE  authority.
 Pick any org unit that has data that will serve as a target. For example, Ngelehun CHC ( DiszpKrYNg8 ). Note down the count of data values:  GET /api/dataValueSets?dataSet=BfMAe6Itzgt&period=202401&orgUnit=DiszpKrYNg8 Now under the same parent (Badija in our example) create a new org unit that will serve as a source. Merge the source into the target with the default strategy in Metadata Management (Organisation units → merge, leave "Move data values to the target organisation unit" selected) or via the API:
 
```POST /api/organisationUnits/merge
{"sources": ["g8upMTyEZGZ"], "target": "DiszpKrYNg8", "deleteSources": true}``` Repeat the request from step 2 for the target. 
Actual
 
The target has 0 data values for Child Health, January 2024: its own 44 values are gone. In general, the target is left with only the values that came from the sources. In this case, since the source was newly created and has no data, Ngelehun CHC loses all of its data.
 
Expected
 
The target still has its 44 values (the source had none to add). In general, the target keeps its own data values and gains the source's values. Where both have a value for the same data element, period, category option combo, and attribute option combo, the most recently updated value wins (as the strategy name and UI say).

nodes.label: Issue DHIS2-22301
nodes.summary: Tracker import 500: NPE in program rule engine when a TE's stored attribute value resolves to null
nodes.description:
Jira Issue DHIS2-22301: Tracker import 500: NPE in program rule engine when a TE's stored attribute value resolves to null
Type: Bug | Status: Planned | Priority: High
Components: [API] Tracker
Description: Explanation
 
A synchronous tracker import fails with an uncaught NPE (HTTP 500) whenever the program rule engine evaluates a tracked entity that has a stored attribute value resolving to  null . Since 2.43.1 this state is created by a perfectly valid import: confidential attribute values are written to the plain  value  column only, leaving  encryptedvalue  NULL — which is also a plaintext-at-rest security regression.
 
Steps to reproduce
 
Verified on 2.43 (rev  8de3dc0 ), Sierra Leone demo,  encryption.password  configured:
 Have a program whose program rules reference a TEI attribute (e.g.  d2:hasValue(#{attr}) ). Have a tracked entity attribute with  confidential=true . POST /api/tracker?async=false  a TE + enrollment in that program including a value for the confidential attribute → 200 OK. POST /api/tracker?async=false  any follow-up for that TE that triggers rule evaluation (e.g. an event for the enrollment, or the enrollment again without the attribute). 
Actual result
 
Step 4 fails with HTTP 500:
 
```java.lang.NullPointerException: Parameter specified as non-null is null: method org.hisp.dhis.rules.models.RuleAttributeValue.<init>, parameter value
  at org.hisp.dhis.rules.models.RuleAttributeValue.<init>(RuleAttributeValue.kt)
  at ...DefaultProgramRuleService.lambda$getAttributes$25(DefaultProgramRuleService.java:441)
  at ...DefaultProgramRuleService.buildEnrollmentsWithEvents(DefaultProgramRuleService.java:367)```
 
Additionally, after step 3 the confidential value is stored  unencrypted  in the  value  column ( encryptedvalue  is NULL), and the export API returns the plaintext.
 
Expected result
 
The import succeeds; the rule engine treats a null/unreadable stored attribute value as absent. Confidential values are stored encrypted.
 
Secondary information
 
Root cause (two layers)
 
1. Unguarded null (the 500).   DefaultProgramRuleService.getAttributes  (2.43, line 441) maps the TE's DB-stored attribute values into  RuleAttributeValue  (Kotlin, non-null  value ) without the null filter the payload side has ( filterNullAttributes ):
 
```trackedEntity.getTrackedEntityAttributeValues().stream()
    .filter(av -> !payloadAttributeUids.contains(av.getAttribute().getUid()))
    .map(av -> new RuleAttributeValue(av.getAttribute().getUid(), av.getValue())); // NPE```
 
getValue()  =  confidential ? encryptedValue : plainValue , so it is null whenever the column backing the attribute's  current  confidential flag is empty.
 
2. How the null state arises.
 
Valid import on 2.43.1+ (main cause, verified):  the Hibernate→JDBC importer migration (DHIS2-21378, first in 2.43.1) introduced  TeavWriter , whose INSERT/UPDATE only touch the plain  value  column —  encryptedvalue  is never written. Its comment assumes master's removal of confidential attributes (DHIS2-21518), which is master-only; on 2.43 the entity/hbm still route confidential reads to  encryptedvalue . Every confidential value imported since 2.43.1 is stored plaintext with  encryptedvalue  NULL → next rule-evaluating import for that TE 500s. Updating a pre-2.43.1 encrypted row also leaves a stale  encryptedvalue  behind, so entity reads silently return the old value. Confidential flag toggled  after values were stored (either direction) — pre-existing footgun, all versions; the value sits in the opposite column.
 
Not causes: missing/short  encryption.password  (import rejected with E1112 before persisting); rotated password (jasypt throws at load, doesn't return null); null payload values (treated as deletion and filtered).
 
Suggested fix
 Null-filter the DB-side stream in  getAttributes  (mirror  filterNullAttributes ) so a null value is "no value" instead of a 500. On 2.43: make  TeavWriter  encrypt confidential values into  encryptedvalue  (or backport the DHIS2-21518 removal). The null-filter alone leaves encryption silently broken. Data repair for rows written since 2.43.1: move plaintext  value  → encrypted  encryptedvalue  for confidential attributes. 
master is unaffected by the storage regression (no  encryptedvalue /confidential routing); the missing null-guard asymmetry predates the 2.43 JDBC migration.
 
Notes
 
Observed in production logs (2026-10-14) on CREATE_AND_UPDATE sync imports. Distinct from the separately-reported  UniqueAttributesSupplier  preheat NPE (caught, WARN-only, no 500). Full repro record: payloads, SQL evidence and both stack variants ( buildEnrollmentsWithEvents:354  payload branch /  :367  saved-enrollment branch) are archived in the task record for this issue.

nodes.label: Issue DHIS2-20446
nodes.summary: Data Entry App - Organization Unit Search Does Not Auto-Expand Hierarchy
nodes.description:
Jira Issue DHIS2-20446: Data Entry App - Organization Unit Search Does Not Auto-Expand Hierarchy
Type: Bug | Status: In Review | Priority: Highest
Components: [App] Data entry
Description: Summary
 
Organization unit search box filters results but does not automatically expand the hierarchy tree to show matching results. Users must manually expand all parent levels to reach the searched organization unit, defeating the purpose of the search functionality.
 
Description
 
Issue Overview
 
The organization unit selector in the Data Entry app has a search box that allows users to type and filter organization units. However, when a user searches for a specific organization unit, the matching results are not automatically revealed in the tree. Instead, users must manually click through each hierarchical level (continent → country → region → district, etc.) to navigate to the organization unit they searched for.
 
This creates a poor user experience because:
 The search functionality appears to work (it filters results) But the filtered results remain hidden behind collapsed tree nodes Users still need to know the full hierarchical path to find their org unit The search doesn't save any time or effort compared to manual navigation 
Current Behavior
 User clicks on "Organisation unit" dropdown showing "Choose a organisation unit" User types organization unit name in the search box (e.g., "Buma") Search box accepts the input and appears to filter Problem:  The organization unit tree structure remains collapsed User must manually expand:
 
Sierra Leone (country level) Bo (region/district level) Bumpe Ngao (chiefdom level) Finally see "Buma MCHP" (facility level) Even though the user already typed "Buma" in the search box 
Expected Behavior
 
When a user types in the organization unit search box:
 Search should filter/match organization units based on the search term All parent nodes in the hierarchy should automatically expand  to reveal matching results Matching organization units should be visible immediately without manual expansion Optionally: matching results should be highlighted or brought to the top of the visible list User should be able to click on the matched organization unit directly from search results 
Steps to Reproduce
 
Test Environment
 
Instance:  DHIS 2 Demo - Sierra Leone - Data Entry Dataset:  Child Health Organization Unit Hierarchy Example:
 
Sierra Leone → Bo → Bumpe Ngao → Buma MCHP
 
Reproduction Steps
 Navigate to Data Entry application Select "Child Health" as the data set Click on "Organisation unit" dropdown (shows "Choose a organisation unit") In the search box at the top, type "Buma" Observe:  The search box accepts the input Observe:  The tree structure still shows only "Sierra Leone" as a collapsed node User must manually expand the hierarchy:
 
Click to expand "Sierra Leone" Click to expand "Bo" Click to expand "Bumpe Ngao" Finally see "Buma MCHP" 
Expected:  After typing "Buma" in step 4, the entire path (Sierra Leone → Bo → Bumpe Ngao → Buma MCHP) should automatically expand and show "Buma MCHP" as a selectable option.
 
Actual:  Search accepts input but does nothing to reveal the matching organization unit. Manual expansion of all parent levels is still required.

nodes.label: Commit 801e071
nodes.author: Jason Pickering
nodes.title: Commit 801e071: perf: use patharray containment for descendant org unit resolution in dataValueSets export (#25261) (#25659)
nodes.message:
GitHub Commit 801e071 by Jason Pickering (2026-10-16T09:30:38+00:00)
Repository: dhis2/dhis2-core
Message: perf: use patharray containment for descendant org unit resolution in dataValueSets export (#25261) (#25659)

* perf: use patharray containment for descendant org unit resolution in dataValueSets export

The ou_with_descendants_ids CTE in HibernateDataExportStore.createExportQuery
resolved descendant org units via `ou.path LIKE root.path || '%'`. Because the
prefix is computed per-row from a joined column rather than a plan-time
constant, Postgres can never use an index for this predicate (not even the
existing varchar_pattern_ops btree on path) and falls back to a full
sequential scan of organisationunit on every call.

Since the org unit path-array migration (DHIS2-22095) added `patharray` plus
a GIN index (organisationunit_patharray_gin), and the DB's own
ou_moved_patharray descendant-update trigger already uses the same
containment idiom, switch this query to `ou.patharray @> root.patharray`.

Live-validated via EXPLAIN ANALYZE against production data (dataValueSets
export with children=true): 260.6ms -> 18.1ms (14.4x), same 643-row result,
seq scan replaced by a Bitmap Index Scan on organisationunit_patharray_gin.

🤖 AI Assisted

* fix: update stale expected SQL in DataExportQueryBuilderTest

The two testFilter_*WithChildren tests still asserted the old
`ou.path LIKE root.path || '%'` join, which no longer matches
the patharray-based descendant containment query.

🤖 AI Assisted

* perf: Match descendant org units on the root UID only

Check `ou.patharray && ARRAY[root.uid]` instead of
`ou.patharray @> root.patharray`. Both are correct, but the latter makes
the GIN scan read the posting list of every ancestor in the root's path,
including the national root, which every org unit contains. For 10
level-4 roots in a 285k-unit hierarchy this takes 4.8ms down to 1.1ms
(961 to 361 buffer hits).

🤖 AI Assisted

---------


(cherry picked from commit 14d432efce124a5f2ccf8ac88ae088ba5758e679)

GitHub Commit fd40e8f by Jason Pickering (2026-10-16T09:29:26+00:00)
Repository: dhis2/dhis2-core
Message: fix: Generate category option combo names from untranslated option names [DHIS2-22281] (#25645)

CategoryOptionCombo.getName() built a missing name from each option's
display name, which is translated into the current user's database
locale. Generated names are persisted (on insert, and by
updateNameIfNotEqual on regeneration), so the stored name followed the
locale of whoever last created, updated or regenerated the category
combo. Use the option names instead.

Existing COCs stored with translated names are renamed back on the
next regeneration.

nodes.label: Issue DHIS2-22299
nodes.summary: [EventVisualization] Add programStage to value
nodes.description:
Jira Issue DHIS2-22299: [EventVisualization] Add programStage to value
Type: Feature | Status: In Progress | Priority: No Priority
Components: [API] Analytics
Description: In  /analytics/events/aggregate , the  value  parameter accepts a stage prefixed data element, e.g.  value=A03MvHHogjR.a3kGcGDCuk6 . When the same value is saved in an EventVisualization, the stage is lost.
 
Current behaviour
 
value  on EventVisualization is not persisted. It is backed by  dataElementValueDimension  or  attributeValueDimension , which only hold the data element or attribute. There is no stage on the value, so a saved value can't tell which stage it belongs to. The visualization-level  programStage  is not enough. In a tracker program the layout can contain dimensions from several stages, and the same data element can be in more than one of them.
 
Example
 
Tracker program with a data element that is in two stages:
 
The app sends  value: { id: <stageId>.<dataElementId> } , which is the same form the analytics API takes. After save and reload,  value  only carries the data element, so the app can't rebuild the  value=<stageId>.<dataElementId>  request.

nodes.label: Issue DHIS2-22300
nodes.summary: Validation rule analysis worker threads block each other on the expression parse-tree cache
nodes.description:
Jira Issue DHIS2-22300: Validation rule analysis worker threads block each other on the expression parse-tree cache
Type: Task | Status: Open | Priority: No Priority
Components: [API] Other
Description: Description
 
When validation rule analysis runs, its worker threads spend a large share of their time blocked or waiting on each other instead of evaluating rules. This shows up in thread dumps and profilers as most validation worker threads parked in the expression parser's cache ( org.hisp.dhis.antlr.cache.LocalCache.get ), and in long total blocked time per analysis. On a production instance (2.43, 20 rules, ~9.8M data values, 16 workers) one 41 s analysis showed 63 s of total blocked time, with 47% of worker samples in this cache.
 
The results of the analysis are correct; the problem is only that the work is serialised.
 
Steps to reproduce
 Use an instance with a reasonably large data set, e.g. the Sierra Leone demo database or a copy of a production database, on a server with several CPU cores. Pick a validation rule group with several rules and a top-level org unit with many descendants. Run validation rule analysis through the API, ideally two at the same time:
 
```POST /api/dataAnalysis/validationRules
Content-Type: application/json

{"ou": "<root org unit UID>", "startDate": "2025-01-01", "endDate": "2025-12-31",
 "vrg": "<validation rule group UID>", "notification": false, "persist": false}```
 
(or Data Quality app > Validation Rule Analysis with the same options). While the analysis is running, take a thread dump of the DHIS2 JVM a few times, e.g.  jcmd <pid> Thread.print , or watch it in a profiler (Glowroot, JFR, IntelliJ). 
Actual
 
Most validation worker threads ( DataValidationRunner  tasks) are  BLOCKED  or  WAITING  inside org.hisp.dhis.antlr.cache.LocalCache.get  / cache2k  put  / expiry-timer code, waiting on one shared lock.
 
Measured on a copy of a 2.43 production database, 2 concurrent analyses, 16 workers:
 
45% of worker thread samples  BLOCKED , 51% inside  LocalCache.get . Production profile of a single 41 s analysis: 63 s total blocked time, 47% of worker samples in  LocalCache.get , 28% parked on the cache lock.
 
Expected
 
Worker threads only touch the shared cache lock when an expression is parsed for the first time; repeated evaluation of an already-parsed expression does not block other workers. Blocked time during validation analysis is close to zero, and analyses run faster when the server has idle CPU.
 
With the fix, on the same database and workload: 0% of worker samples blocked, 1% in  LocalCache.get , identical results (same violations), and 2 concurrent analyses about 7% faster per round on 12 cores (8.63 s -> 8.03 s).

nodes.label: Issue DHIS2-21925
nodes.summary: Visualization fails to open (500) when data dimension item sort order has a gap
nodes.description:
Jira Issue DHIS2-21925: Visualization fails to open (500) when data dimension item sort order has a gap
Type: Bug | Status: In Progress | Priority: No Priority
Components: [API] Metadata model
Description: Affected versions
 
Confirmed live on  2.41  (production instance). The code path ( VisualizationController , Visualization.hbm.xml ) is unchanged in structure on current  master  (2.43-dev), so this likely affects all currently supported branches. Not yet audited version-by-version.
 
Summary
 
If the  sort_order  values for a visualization's data dimension items ( visualization_datadimensionitems  table) contain a gap — i.e. are not a contiguous  0..n-1 sequence — the visualization fails to open (or appear in any list response) with an unhandled NullPointerException , returned to the client as an HTTP 500 with no useful error message.
 
This is not a data-visualizer-only bug: it affects  any  API call that returns the affected visualization in a list or as a single object, including the "Open" dialog's search/browse list, direct  GET /api/visualizations/{uid} , and dashboards that embed the visualization.
 
Steps to reproduce
 Create a visualization with 3+ data dimension items. Directly manipulate the  sort_order  column of one of its rows in visualization_datadimensionitems  to introduce a gap (e.g. change  0, 1, 2  to  0, 1, 3 ). (In the production incident that surfaced this, something already in the system produced this gap organically — the exact code path that allows it has not yet been identified. See "Root cause of the corruption" below.) Attempt to open the visualization in Data Visualizer, or  GET /api/visualizations/{uid}?fields=... , or list visualizations with that one included in the result page. Observe HTTP 500 with an empty/unhelpful error body. 
Root cause (of the crash)
 
VisualizationController.postProcessResponseEntities()  / postProcessResponseEntity()  unconditionally call addExpressionDimensionItemElementsToDataDimensionItems(visualization)  for every visualization returned by the API. That method does:
 
```// VisualizationController.java:203-204
visualization.getDataDimensionItems().stream()
    .filter(ddi -> ddi.getExpressionDimensionItem() != null)```
 
visualization.getDataDimensionItems()  is backed by a Hibernate  indexed  <list>  mapping ( Visualization.hbm.xml:121-127 ,  <list-index column="sort_order" base="0"/> ). Hibernate reconstructs this list by allocating an array of size  max(sort_order) + 1  and placing each row at its  sort_order  index. If the  sort_order  sequence for a visualization has a gap, the missing index is silently left as a  null  array element —  no exception is raised when the entity loads . The NPE only surfaces later, here, when the stream tries to call .getExpressionDimensionItem()  on the null element:
 
```java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "org.hisp.dhis.common.DataDimensionItem.getExpressionDimensionItem()" because "ddi" is null
    at org.hisp.dhis.webapi.controller.VisualizationController.lambda$addExpressionDimensionItemElementsToDataDimensionItems$1(VisualizationController.java:204)
    ...
    at org.hisp.dhis.webapi.controller.VisualizationController.postProcessResponseEntities(VisualizationController.java:152)
    at org.hisp.dhis.webapi.controller.AbstractFullReadOnlyController.getObjectList(AbstractFullReadOnlyController.java:240)```
 
Why the error is invisible in the logs
 
CrudControllerAdvice.defaultExceptionHandler  — the catch-all  @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) for anything not covered by the ~40 typed handlers above it — does:
 
```@ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)
public WebMessage defaultExceptionHandler(Exception ex) {
  ex.printStackTrace();
  return error(getExceptionMessage(ex));
}```
 
printStackTrace()  writes to raw  stderr , completely bypassing SLF4J/log4j2. This means the exception never reaches  dhis.log  at any log level, and depending on the deployment's log pipeline, may show up as a bare, contextless one-line entry with no stack trace at all (this is what happened in production — the only visible symptom was a single log line reading java.lang.NullPointerException , with no message and no trace, making the underlying bug very difficult to diagnose without direct access to raw, unprocessed stderr). This should be fixed separately (replace  ex.printStackTrace()  with a proper  log.error("...", ex)  call) so future unhandled exceptions are actually diagnosable.
 
Root cause of the corruption (not yet identified)
 
The  sort_order  gap itself must originate from some code path that removes a data dimension item from a visualization's list without renumbering the remaining rows. This has not yet been traced — candidates are the visualization update/PATCH handler, or a metadata import/merge path. In the production instance where this was found, 13 visualizations were affected, each missing exactly one index (confirmed via SQL, no duplicate  sort_order  values found, ruling out a different corruption mechanism).
 
Immediate mitigation (data repair, already applied in the reported instance)
 
```begin;
with fix as (
  select ctid,
         row_number() over (partition by visualizationid order by sort_order) - 1 as new_sort_order
  from visualization_datadimensionitems
  where visualizationid in (<affected ids>)
)
update visualization_datadimensionitems v
set sort_order = fix.new_sort_order
from fix
where v.ctid = fix.ctid;
commit;```
 
Followed by  POST /api/maintenance?cacheClear=true  to flush Hibernate's L2 cache (the mapping has <cache usage="read-write"/> , and a direct-SQL fix bypasses Hibernate, so the running app would otherwise keep serving the stale, gapped collection from cache).
 
Proposed fix (this ticket)
 
Two parts, already drafted/implemented against  master  pending a ticket number to branch from:
 Data integrity check  (defensive/detective, ships regardless of root cause fix): a new yaml check,  analytical_objects/visualizations_wrong_sort_order.yaml , modeled directly on the existing  option_sets/option_sets_wrong_sort_order.yaml  pattern, flags any visualization whose visualization_datadimensionitems.sort_order  sequence has a gap. Severity  CRITICAL  (this causes a hard application error, unlike the option-sets version which is  INFO /cosmetic). Defensive code fix  (not yet written):  .filter(Objects::nonNull)  before the existing filter at  VisualizationController.java:203-204 , so a future gap degrades gracefully (skips the corrupted item) instead of 500ing the entire request. 
Still open / follow-up tickets to consider:
 
Find and fix the actual deletion/update path that allows the  sort_order  gap to occur in the first place. Fix  CrudControllerAdvice.defaultExceptionHandler 's use of raw  printStackTrace()  so future unhandled exceptions are diagnosable via normal logging. MapView.hbm.xml  has the byte-identical  dataDimensionItems  list mapping ( mapview_datadimensionitems  table) — worth checking whether the same class of corruption can occur there, and whether a companion data integrity check is warranted.
 
Evidence
 
Glowroot trace and raw catalina.out capture from the reporting instance (available on request, not attached here — contains internal hostnames/session data). SQL confirmation of the gap on the reporting instance's  visualization_datadimensionitems  table (13 affected visualizations, each short by exactly one index). Direct SQL verification of the new data integrity check's  summary_sql / details_sql  against a clean Postgres instance, confirming correct detection of a seeded gap and no false positives on clean data.

Jira Issue DHIS2-22252: [Event] [A] Analytics cache key ignores program stage and enrollment org unit
Type: Bug | Status: In Review | Priority: No Priority
Components: [API] Analytics
Description: When analytics caching is enabled,  /analytics/events/aggregate  can return a cached response from a different request. This happens because the cache key leaves out the program stage of stage-prefixed items and all enrollment org unit ( ENROLLMENT_OU ) parameters.
 
Cause
 QueryItem.getProgramStageUid()  returns the program UID, not the stage UID ( dhis-api/.../common/QueryItem.java , line 230):
 
```private String getProgramStageUid() {
  return program != null ? program.getUid() : null;
}```
 
The  programStageItem  part of the key is therefore the same for every stage of a program, so items from different stages (e.g.  A03MvHHogjR.ou  and  ZzYYXq4fJie.ou ) produce the same key. EventQueryParams.getKey()  leaves out all  enrollmentOu*  fields ( dhis-service-analytics/.../event/EventQueryParams.java , line 630).  enrollmentOuDimensionItems ,  enrollmentOuFilterItems ,  enrollmentOuDimensionLevels ,  enrollmentOuFilterLevels  and  enrollmentOuDimensionHierarchical  are not added to the key. The equivalent  registrationOu*  fields are added. 
Examples
 
dimension=ZzYYXq4fJie.ou:USER_ORGUNIT  returned the cached result of an earlier  A03MvHHogjR.ou:USER_ORGUNIT  request, including that stage's header name. filter=ENROLLMENT_OU:O6uvpzGd5pu  returned the cached response of the same request without that filter, so the filter was not applied.
 
Expected
 
The cache key should include the program stage UID of stage-prefixed query items and all enrollment org unit dimension and filter parameters, in the same way as  registrationOu* .

nodes.summary: Add BMI-for-age z-score function (0–19 years) to the rule engine
nodes.description:
Jira Issue DHIS2-22297: Add BMI-for-age z-score function (0–19 years) to the rule engine
Type: Feature | Status: Open | Priority: No Priority
Components: [API] Program rules, [Core] Expression Language
Description: Context
 
Part of ROADMAP-627 (extend z-score–based nutritional assessment to 5–19 years). Complements DHIS2-21993, which extends  d2:zScoreHFA  (5–19) and  d2:zScoreWFA  (5–10) using the WHO 2007 Growth Reference.
 
DHIS2-21993 explicitly leaves a gap:  weight-for-height does not exist in the WHO reference for 5–19 years — WHO uses BMI-for-age instead.  Without a BMI-for-age function, implementations cannot automatically classify thinness, overweight or obesity for school-aged children and adolescents, which is the core indicator for school health programs.
 
Requested by Egypt (MoH, school health program). They already run a well-baby tracker (<5) with automated z-scores (WFA, HFA, WFH), decision support and the growth chart widget, and want the same experience extended to 5–19 for the school health app, plus BMI curves given rising obesity trends. Today nurses classify manually or with paper-based tools, which introduces errors. Requested timeline: Oct–Nov 2026.
 
Proposal
 
Add a new z-score function for  BMI-for-age  (e.g.  d2:zScoreBFA ), with male/female variants, implemented in the shared expression-parser / rule engine (backend, web and Android).
 
Reference tables (WHO, use the  Simplified field tables  to keep the same structure as the existing tables in  ZScoreTable.kt ):
 
0–5 years:  WHO Child Growth Standards (2006) – BMI-for-age: https://www.who.int/tools/child-growth-standards/standards/body-mass-index-for-age-bmi-for-age 5–19 years:  WHO Growth Reference (2007) – BMI-for-age: https://www.who.int/tools/growth-reference-data-for-5to19-years/indicators/bmi-for-age
 
Tables file: https://github.com/dhis2/expression-parser/blob/main/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/hisp/dhis/lib/expression/math/ZScoreTable.kt
 
Acceptance criteria
 
New function returns the BMI-for-age z-score for ages 0–19 years, male and female, consistent with the existing z-score functions (range -3 to +3, same rounding/behaviour). Works in program rules on backend, Capture web app and Android (shared rule engine). Results validated against WHO reference values / WHO AnthroPlus for a sample of ages and sexes (see also DHIS2-22201 on discrepancies with WHO calculations). Documented in the program rules / expression functions docs, including the WHO cut-offs implementers typically use (5–19: thinness < -2 SD, severe thinness < -3 SD, overweight > +1 SD, obesity > +2 SD).
 
Open questions
 
Function input: BMI value directly, or weight + height (computing BMI inside the function)? Keep the signature consistent with  d2:zScoreWFA(ageInMonths, weight, gender) . Age unit for 5–19 (WHO 2007 tables are in months) — confirm same convention as DHIS2-21993.
 
Out of scope
 
Extending the Capture growth chart widget/plugin to 5–19 and adding BMI curves (also requested by Egypt) — to be tracked separately under ROADMAP-627.

Jira Issue DHIS2-21993: Extend the range of zscore functions up to 19 years old
Type: Feature | Status: In Review | Priority: High
Components: [API] Program rules, [Core] Expression Language
Description: The d2:zscore functions are limited to the range 0-5 years old. These functions are only used in the Program rules (not supported in Program Indicator expressions). The program rule engine is a shared library used by backend, web and Android, so this functionality only has to be implemented in this shared Rule Engine.
 
The evaluation of zscore is based on a predefined tables located in the expression-parser. These tables are copy/pasted from the WHO recommendation. This recommendation is split into two segments: 0-5 years and 5-19 years. Currently, the expression-parser only includes the segment 0-5 years, so the purpose of this feature is to extend the support by including the 5-19 years reference.
 
There are three zscore functions ( d2:zScoreHFA ,  d2:zScoreWFA  and  d2:zScoreWFH ), each of them having the variants  male  and  female , so there are six tables in total.
 
The tables are defined in this file in the expression-parser:
 

 
These tables include the values in the range (-3, 3), which correspond with the extended tables of WHO ( tables for 0-5 years ).
 
For the range 5-19 years, the WHO has a reference that can be found here (use the  Simplified field tables  to get the same data structure as in the expression-parser):
 
Height-for-age:  available in the range 5-19 Weight-for-age:  available in the range 5-10 Weight-for-height:  not available. It uses BMI-for-age, which is not the same.

Jira Issue DHIS2-22112: Program rules are not evaluated in event/enrollment forms opened without an organisation unit selected
Type: Bug | Status: Done | Priority: High
Components: [App] Capture
Description: Steps to reproduce
 
Event program:
 Open Capture Program → "Antenatal care visit".  Leave "Organisation unit" unselected. Click Create new event (The form opens with Organisation unit = None selected) Note the WHOMCH Smoking cessation counselling provided field is visible (it should be hidden by its rule). In WHOMCH Hemoglobin value, enter 5.
 
Actual:  no warning appears; rules are not evaluated. Expected:  "Hemoglobin value lower than normal" warning shows (as it does in 106.6.2). Now pick any facility in the form's Organisation unit field (e.g. Ngelehun CHC).
 
The warning appears immediately and the smoking-cessation field hides → rules now evaluate. 
Tracker-program variant: Select a tracker program (e.g. Child Programme) →  "See working list without organisation unit"  → open a person → add/edit an event.  The form loads with no org unit and rules stay silent (e.g. the low-APGAR comment warning doesn't fire) until an org unit is set.
 
Original report: Program rules are not being evaluated or executed in Tracker programs when using Capture App from 106.6.3.
 
The same program rules, metadata, DHIS2 server and test cases work correctly when Capture App 106.6.2 is installed. After upgrading Capture to 106.6.3, the program rule actions are no longer applied.
 
This affects the business logic configured in the Tracker programs, including conditional field behavior, validations and other actions triggered by values entered in tracked entity attributes or program-stage data elements.
 
Preconditions
 
A Tracker program containing at least one enabled program rule. The program rule has a valid condition and an enabled program rule action. The rule can be reproduced successfully using Capture App 106.6.2.
 
Steps to Reproduce
 Install or enable Capture App 106.6.3 onwards. Select a Tracker program containing previously validated program rules. Create a new tracked entity or open an existing enrollment. Enter or modify a value that satisfies a program rule condition. Observe whether the configured program rule action is applied. Downgrade Capture App to version 106.6.2. Repeat the same steps using the same DHIS2 server, metadata, user and test case. 
Actual Result
 
in Capture App from 106.6.3, the program rule condition does not produce the configured action. The program rules appear not to be evaluated or executed.
 
No changes were made to the program rule metadata between the tests.
 
Expected Result
 
Program rules should be evaluated whenever the relevant tracked entity attribute or program-stage data element changes. When the rule condition evaluates to true, the corresponding action should be applied.
 
The behavior should be consistent with Capture App 106.6.2.
 
Regression evidence
 
Capture App 106.6.2: program rules work as expected. Capture App 106.6.3: the same program rules do not execute. Both tests use the same DHIS2 environment and program metadata. Reinstalling version 106.6.2 restores the expected behavior.
 
Capture app versions 106.7.8, 107.0.5, 107.0.10 shows the same error.

nodes.label: Commit 55bfcba
nodes.author: Jason Pickering
nodes.title: Commit 55bfcba: fix: Keep the target's data values and approvals in an org unit merge [DHIS2-22296] (#25734)
nodes.message:
GitHub Commit 55bfcba by Jason Pickering (2026-10-15T09:03:58+00:00)
Repository: dhis2/dhis2-core
Message: fix: Keep the target's data values and approvals in an org unit merge [DHIS2-22296] (#25734)

With the LAST_UPDATED strategy (the default, shown in Metadata Management
as "Move data values to the target organisation unit") the merge first
deleted all of the target's data values and data approvals, then copied in
the most recent source rows only. Values only the target had were lost, and
where both had a value the source always won, contrary to the UI's "the
most recently updated is kept". The deletes were hard deletes and were not
audited.

Rank the target's own rows together with the sources' rows and upsert the
winners into the target, then delete the source rows. On a tie the target
keeps its own row; a tie between sources goes to the lowest org unit id so
the result is repeatable. Replayed on a copy of a production database:
target 336 values -> 349 (its own plus 13 new keys from the source), every
key holding the newest value from either side; previously 336 -> 61.

nodes.title: Commit 4de3a02: fix: Do not load unloaded collections when building metadata audit entries [DHIS2-22235] (#25534)
nodes.message:
GitHub Commit 4de3a02 by Jason Pickering (2026-10-13T16:20:19+00:00)
Repository: dhis2/dhis2-core
Message: fix: Do not load unloaded collections when building metadata audit entries [DHIS2-22235] (#25534)

* fix: Do not load unloaded collections when building metadata audit entries [DHIS2-22235]

createAuditEntry treated an unloaded PersistentCollection like an entity
proxy and read it, so every update of a data set or org unit group loaded
all of its org units after commit just to list their UIDs in the audit
entry. This breaks the method's documented rule 2 ("Do not include any lazy
HibernateProxy or PersistentCollection that is not loaded"). A collection
the request did not load is now left out; loaded collections are still
written as before.

On a copy of a production database, changing only the sharing of a data
set or org unit group with ~138k org units went from 2.7-3.3 s and a
~1.9 MB audit entry to 0.03-0.16 s and ~1 KB.

🤖 AI Assisted

* fix: Write loaded empty collections as [] in metadata audit entries [DHIS2-22235]

Review feedback: with unloaded collections left out, a loaded collection that the request
emptied was also missing from the entry (putValueToMap dropped empty collections), so
"removed every org unit" and "changed only the sharing" produced the same entry. A loaded
empty collection is now written as [], so a missing key only means "not loaded". This
matches the delete path, which already writes empty collections.

Also moves the unloaded-collection check into a helper to keep createAuditEntry within
the cognitive complexity limit.

nodes.author: Jason Pickering
nodes.title: Commit 741c282: perf: Speed up COC regeneration [DHIS2-22203] (#25468)
nodes.message:
GitHub Commit 741c282 by Jason Pickering (2026-10-13T08:19:19+00:00)
Repository: dhis2/dhis2-core
Message: perf: Speed up COC regeneration [DHIS2-22203] (#25468)

* perf: Make category option combo regeneration linear in the number of combos

Regenerating the option combos of a large category combo (e.g. 5000 x 2 options, 10,000
combos) took ~15s, and was slower on master than on 2.41:

- each persisted option combo was matched by scanning all generated option combos
- each persisted option combo's category options were lazy loaded one query at a time
- every generated option combo was linked back onto its category options, lazy loading
  each option's full set of option combos, including for combos that already existed
- a generated option combo computed its name on every getName() call by scanning each
  category's option list

Generated option combos are now indexed by their category options, the persisted option
combos are preloaded with their options, only added option combos are linked back to their
options, and generated option combos are named once when generated.

🤖 AI Assisted

* test: Cover category option combo regeneration query count and naming

- regenerating the option combos of a category combo must not lazy load per option combo
  (15 vs 60 option combos give the same number of per-row loads)
- regeneration adds the combos of a new option, deletes them when it is removed, and a
  repeated run changes nothing
- generated option combos are named exactly as an unnamed option combo computes its name,
  including an option shared by two categories

🤖 AI Assisted

* refactor: Split up category option combo regeneration for Sonar

Moves the generated option combo index into a record and the add-if-missing step into its
own method, to reduce cognitive complexity and keep the indexing loop separate from the add
loop. No behaviour change.

🤖 AI Assisted

* perf: Skip needless session flushes when regenerating category option combos

The preload queries only read, but each one auto flushed first, dirty
